title: Batch germination stop and priority drift — remediation playbook
creator: Maya Patel
description: Summary: During a regional capacity drain on 2025-11-03 we observed repeated 95th/99th percentile tail latency spikes tied to prolonged pauses in batch formation (internally observed as 'batch germination stop') and a correlated drift in per-request priority ordering that caused lower-priority traffic to preempt higher-priority routes. Impact: several customer endpoints experienced token-latency degradations (2x P95, 4x P99) for ~18 minutes across two AZs; no data loss but a material SLA blip for Dedicated customers. Scope: affected continuous-batching service in region us-west-2 on machines running kernel-profile v1.21 with affinity refresh enabled.
timeline:
2025-11-03 09:12 UTC - First alerts from synthetic traces and Console latency dashboard.
2025-11-03 09:15 UTC - Pager duty on-call ack; triage shows sudden drop in batch formation rate despite steady request ingress.
2025-11-03 09:20 UTC - Temporary capacity rebalancer triggered and started moving work; tail latency worsened.
2025-11-03 09:28 UTC - Manual fallback to smaller-window coalescing rule applied, which recovered P95 within ~4 minutes.
2025-11-03 09:35 UTC - Full traffic routing rollback to pre-drain policy; incident declared resolved by 09:45 UTC.
2025-11-04 to 2025-11-20 - Investigation and mitigations documented below.
observed_signals:
- Batch formation rate dropped by ~70% for 12 contiguous minutes in two AZs.
- Active batch count per worker plateaued with high per-batch idle slots.
- Priority reorder metric (priority_reschedule_ratio) increased 3x during event.
- KV-cache hit ration unchanged.
- Autoscaler showed transient under-provisioning in the impacted subpool because of aggressive bin-packing during drain.
root_cause_analysis: Primary cause: an interaction between the region-level capacity drain (AWS rolling maintenance) and the adaptive affinity refresh logic. When nodes were marked draining, the affinity refresh aggressively rebalanced long-lived cohorts which temporarily removed eligible requests from active slot consideration; combined with the new 'sparse-window shrink' heuristic in runtime-1.21 this led the batching coordinator to repeatedly delay forming batches awaiting missing cohort members (batch germination stop).\nSecondary cause: a priority-reschedule side-effect: requests re-enqueued during affinity refresh received new ephemeral priorities that drifted lower relative to steady traffic, producing fairness inversion where background workloads intermittently leapfrogged higher-priority routes.\nWhy safeguards failed: existing drain-handling assumed immediate eviction of inflight cohorts; the adaptive window shrink introduced a timing dependency that wasn't covered by unit tests or load-stage chaos scenarios.
mitigations_applied_during_incident: - Rolled back sparse-window shrink heuristic (hotfix runtime-1.21 -> runtime-1.20 behavior) to stop batched waits.\n- Applied short-lived policy: treat draining nodes as 'evict-immediately' for batch membership rather than waiting for affinity refresh.\n- Temporarily restricted autoscaler bin-packing aggressiveness to prevent under-provisioning during AZ maintenance windows.
long_term_action_items: (A1) Implement a 'batching-drain-mode' flag that signals the batching coordinator to avoid cohort-based waits when any node in pool is draining — owner: Aaron Li — estimate: 3
(A2) Add deterministic priority-stability token when re-enqueuing requests so transient requeues preserve original priority buckets — owner: Priya Nair — estimate: 2
(A3) Extend chaos tests: add rolling-drain scenarios with affinity-refresh + sparse-window shrink enabled to CI perf suite — owner: SRE Team (Jonas Meyer) — estimate: 3
(A4) Add dashboard alert for 'batch-formation-rate / expected-ingress' ratio dropping below 0.6 for >60s with automated paging — owner: Observability (Rashmi Rao) — estimate: 1

(A5) Post-deploy canary for any heuristic that alters batch-windowing: run small-percentage workload for 15 minutes and validate P95/P99 against baseline before ramping — owner: Platform Releases — estimate: 2

(A6) Documentation: update runbook for 'capacity drain' to include immediate check of affinity refresh + window heuristics and steps to trigger fast rollback — owner: Aaron Li & Maya Patel — estimate: 1
acceptance_criteria:
- Flag 'batching-drain-mode' implemented and tested with unit + integration coverage.
- Priority-stability token in place; no observable priority_reschedule_ratio spike in simulated requeue tests.
- New chaos test consistently reproduces prior behaviour in CI before code merges.
- Dashboard alert fires in staging during simulated degradation and it pages on-call.
- Runbook changes reviewed and acknowledged by SRE and Runtime teams.
monitoring_and_dashboards:
- New metric: batch_germination_rate (batches_started / expected_batches) added to Console.
- New alert: batch_germination_rate < 0.6 for 60s -> PAGER.
- Priority-stability ratio chart added to per-region latency dashboard.
- Synthetic canaries updated to emulate cohort drift during drains.
risk_and_rollout_plan: Rollout plan for batching-drain-mode: feature gated behind 'batching_drain_mode' flag. Canary rollout at 2% traffic for 6 hours in eu-west-1, monitor batch_germination_rate, P95, P99 and priority_reschedule_ratio. If regressions appear revert flag. Full rollout after 48h stable canary.\nRisk: incomplete handling could increase small-batch formation frequency and raise overall token cost; mitigation: telemetry to track tokens/second and autoremove flag if token-cost increases > 12%.
comments: 2025-11-05 Maya Patel: Initial investigation shows strong correlation with affinity refresh churn during node drains. Working with SRE to get drain logs.
2025-11-06 Aaron Li: Prototyped disabling sparse-window shrink locally; repro rate dropped in night-run. Drafting hotfix PR.
2025-11-07 Jonas Meyer (SRE): Confirmed AWS maintenance schedule overlapped incident; SRE will add a 'drain-gating' step to maintenance playbook.
2025-11-12 Priya Nair: Design for priority-stability token sketched. Needs API-level review to avoid altering observable priority semantics.
2025-11-18 Rashmi Rao: Observability PR merged with new charts; added synthetic canary for cohort-drain scenario.
2025-11-20 Aaron Li: Draft playbook attached; opening ticket for implementation of A1/A2. Planning canary next week.
